Its own script, not the captions: one paragraph per beat explaining what is on screen, in the order the picture builds, every sentence restating the lesson's own text (fitnessData.ts: INTRO_TEXT, DEFINITION_TEXT, POWER_CONCEPT, MODULE_COPY, SKILLS, ARCHETYPES, HOPPER_DOMAINS, ENERGY_SYSTEMS, ENERGY_BENCHMARKS, CONTINUUM_EXAMPLES) and the captions, no new facts or numbers; each beat names its passage. The voice is Charon. Edit a sentence and narration-check fails until its clip is regenerated (voice/ pipeline), copied into public/narration/fitness/intro/ and node scripts/narration-manifest.mjs has run. Plain hyphens only.

title.text: What is fitness? In the CrossFit Journal, in October two thousand two, Greg Glassman set out to do what he argued no authority had bothered to do: give a clear, usable, measurable definition of fitness.

models.source: INTRO_TEXT s2; MODULE_COPY skills, hopper, pathways and continuum (first sentences)
models.text: He built it from four complementary models and one definition. First, ten general physical skills. Then the hopper, a drum of random challenges. Three metabolic engines, the energy systems. And a continuum, from sickness, through wellness, to fitness.

definition.text: And the definition: fitness is work capacity across broad time and modal domains. Plot power output against the duration of the effort. Average it across many tasks, and the area under the resulting curve is your fitness.

lifetime.source: INTRO_TEXT last clause; MODULE_COPY health s1 to s3
lifetime.text: Now add a whole life. Stretch that curve back through every age, and it becomes a surface. Sustain that capacity across a lifetime, and it is health: the volume you keep under the surface.

map.text: This lesson walks through each model, as presented in the original article and the official CrossFit Level 1 Training Guide. Skills, the hopper, energy, capacity, the continuum, and health. Six interactive models. Pick any one to begin.
